data.title: Analyst Maintains Buy on Contineum, Trims Price Target to $23 Following PIPE-307 Setback While PIPE-791 IPF Program Remains Core Value Driver
data.description:
Gaurav Maini, an analyst from LifeSci Capital, maintained the Buy rating on Contineum Therapeutics, Inc. Class A. The associated price target was lowered to $23.00.

Gaurav Maini has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, primarily centered on Contineum’s wholly owned lead program PIPE-791 for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, which he continues to view as the core source of shareholder value. The recent failure of JNJ-5120/PIPE-307 to hit its Phase 2 primary endpoint in major depressive disorder is seen as the loss of an upside lever rather than a change to the fundamental thesis, since the Street and his model had assigned limited value to this out-licensed asset.

Maini also points to a still-attractive risk‑reward profile supported by a sizable ongoing Phase 2 PROPEL-IPF trial and an important upcoming class read-through from Bristol Myers Squibb’s Phase 3 ALOFT-IPF study, which could validate the LPAR1 antagonist mechanism. After removing PIPE-307 from his valuation, he modestly lowers his price target to $23, yet maintains a Buy rating, reflecting confidence that PIPE-791’s potential and Contineum’s existing cash runway can drive meaningful upside from current levels despite the setback in the partnered program.

data.title: Empire Hold Rating Maintained as Price Target Trimmed to C$52 Amid Mixed Operating Trends and Modest Valuation Reset
data.description:
Analyst from TD Cowen maintained a Hold rating on Empire Co Cl A NV and decreased the price target to C$52.00 from C$53.00.

analyst has given his Hold rating due to a combination of factors, including mixed operating trends and a modestly reduced valuation outlook, reflected in the revised price target of C$52 from C$53. Quarterly earnings matched expectations, but softer-than-hoped food sales and comparable growth suggest Empire’s core retail momentum is not yet fully aligned with the strongest peers.

At the same time, management is still guiding to EPS growth near the top of its 8%-11% range, relying meaningfully on cost efficiencies and one-time benefits rather than robust sales-driven expansion. Empire’s heavy conventional store mix leaves it less leveraged to discount, pharmacy, and e-commerce, creating a competitive headwind, though solid free cash flow generation offers downside support and justifies maintaining, rather than upgrading, the current Hold stance.

data.title: Analyst Reaffirms Buy on Contineum, Highlighting PIPE-791 IPF Upside Despite Muscarinic MDD Trial Setback
data.description:
William Blair analyst Myles Minter has reiterated their bullish stance on CTNM stock, giving a Buy rating on September 3.

Myles Minter has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors tied to Contineum’s core value driver rather than the recent trial setback. While the muscarinic program for major depressive disorder failed its Phase II primary endpoint and has been removed from his model, he had already assigned a modest success probability and viewed that asset as higher risk with limited clinical validation.

data.title: Transat Price Target Cut to C$2.00 as Delayed Earnings Normalization Leaves Risk/Reward Balanced, Supporting Hold Rating
data.description:

analyst has given his Hold rating due to a combination of factors reflecting both structural challenges and longer-term potential. Transat’s focus on price-sensitive vacation travelers, thin margins, and elevated leverage leave earnings highly exposed to competition, flat yields, and a sharp rise in fuel costs, which together constrain near-term profitability and justify a more cautious stance.

At the same time, the analyst sees meaningful upside if industry conditions normalize, supported by a strong brand, expected margin gains from fleet ramp-up, cabin changes, and a new loyalty program, as well as continued government backing that stabilizes the balance sheet. The price target cut to C$2.00, driven by higher amortization and interest expense, reflects delayed earnings normalization to F2030, while a 10x P/E on that out-year EPS suggests the risk/reward profile is balanced rather than compelling, supporting a Hold recommendation.

data.title: Thunder Gold: Strong Tower Mountain Drill Results Support 5Moz Target; Riley Venton Reiterates Buy with $0.60 Price Target
data.description:
Analyst Riley Venton of Atrium Research maintained a Buy rating on Thunder Gold, with a price target of C$0.60.

Riley Venton has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, chiefly the strong drilling results from hole TM23-137X at the Bench Target, which significantly extend known mineralization at Tower Mountain. The new assays show long, continuous intercepts with consistent grades, much of which lies beneath the current pit shell, indicating meaningful potential to convert Inferred resources to Indicated and add new ounces in the upcoming resource estimate.

These results follow a series of deep holes over the past month that collectively demonstrate the robustness and scalability of the mineralized system, reinforcing confidence in Thunder Gold’s ability to reach or surpass its higher-confidence ~5Moz target. On this basis, and given the implications for future resource growth and valuation, Venton is maintaining a Buy recommendation along with a target price of $0.60 per share, reflecting expected upside as the updated mineral resource is delivered.
